tool_change.scope: the precision resolver gains an evidence layer and per-site evidence classes; the ordinary test suite and the normal-source tree are unchanged

classes.encoding: at the dlsym call the interpreter reads the NUL-terminated identifier at the pointer in %rsi from the exact image, checks the candidate's dynamic export index, and models the return as ('sym', name); the subsequent store/load/call then resolves to that named exported symbol
classes.invariant: the second argument is a single in-image address holding an identifier and the candidate exports the name; a computed, loaded or multi-valued argument is not evidence and leaves the site unresolved
classes.negative_control: self-test: dlsym TOP argument, symbolic argument and non-string address each return None; the ordinary site stays unresolved

classes.mechanism: Rust std/core trait-object and runtime-hook dispatch
classes.encoding: a site whose enclosing symbol is in the linked core/std image is resolved to the address-taken functions of that image
classes.invariant: these are compiler-constructed vtables and runtime hooks (fmt Write/Debug/Drop, the panic hook, Once, libc/syscall weak pointers, the libunwind trace callback); the only code that writes such a slot is the same std/core routine, so no application-supplied OpenSSL callback can be a member
classes.negative_control: self-test: a core-named site resolves; an application-named site is not given R2 and stays unresolved

classes.encoding: the tool re-reads the table from the exact candidate: PMETH_STANDARD_METHODS (10 x 8-byte entries), DEFAULT_CONF_METHOD.load_bio (DEFAULT_METHOD+0x10), the EvpCamelliaKey.block store set, the static ASN1_TEMPLATE/ASN1_ADB entries the resolver could follow, and the default EC_KEY_METHOD table; an entry that is zero, unreadable or a non-code value is reported incomplete
classes.invariant: every admitted entry is a relocation-resolved in-image function pointer; a table with an unfilled or non-code entry is not evidence-complete
classes.negative_control: self-test: a table with a non-code third entry reports that entry incomplete

classes.encoding: left unresolved as ABI_OPEN_PROVIDER_CONFIG; the in-image built-in provider remains the conservative target bound but is not claimed complete
classes.invariant: the immediate callee of a fetch/method-store site is a built-in provider implementation, but the target set can grow through a provider module named by a configuration file
classes.negative_control: the class is not applied as resolved; every A1 site is counted in precision.abi_open.provider_config

classes.encoding: resolved to the in-image link-time method-table entries only when the workload imports no setter for EVP_PKEY_METHOD/EVP_MD/EVP_CIPHER/BIO_METHOD/UI_METHOD/X509_LOOKUP_METHOD/CONF_METHOD
classes.invariant: the dispatched table is a built-in table in the image and the workload cannot install an entry through any of those public setter families
classes.negative_control: self-test: the same A2 site stays unresolved when the workload imports EVP_MD_meth_new

classes.encoding: the interpreter marks a load from runtime::mem MALLOC_FN/REALLOC_FN/FREE_FN; the three audited reachable sites are recorded as ABI_OPEN_CONFIG_BOUND and are never resolved
classes.invariant: the public CRYPTO_set_mem_functions ABI admits any caller-supplied triple; the NULL globals in this configuration are a runtime fact, not a static bound
classes.negative_control: self-test: the O1 site stays unresolved after the evidence pass

tool_change.residual_bound_note: a resolved evidence-class site keeps the resolver's previous conservative residual contribution (taken_code + reachable field stores + unknown call-argument targets) as part of its target set, so the closure's reachability upper bound is preserved rather than narrowed by the new evidence

per_class.invariant: the literal names an exported candidate symbol; the dlsym result is that symbol
the linked core/std image; no application callback
link-time constant table entries read from the exact image
ABI_OPEN_PROVIDER_CONFIG: config-driven external provider loading is reachable
per_class.note: the audited 25 remain open; one additional provider-dispatch site became reachable through the improved graph and is also open

per_class.invariant: built-in EVP_PKEY_METHOD/EVP_MD/EVP_CIPHER/BIO_METHOD/UI_METHOD/X509_LOOKUP_METHOD/CONF_METHOD tables; no setter for those families is imported
ABI_OPEN_CONFIG_BOUND: the public allocator-override ABI is not statically bounded

new_reachable_site.why: the improved dlsym/table targets made this provider cipher function reachable from the workload; it is not one of the audit's 135/132

classification_result.dlsym_missing_note: the one literal that names no candidate export is glibc's __pthread_get_minstack, looked up inside the linked std thread runtime. The site is R2-bounded (std/core) and the target is a libc hook, not an application callback. The resolver records the missing export and does not fabricate an export-index target for it.

A1.why: SSL_CTX_new_ex calls OPENSSL_init_ssl(OPENSSL_INIT_LOAD_SSL_STRINGS), which in this candidate unconditionally adds OPENSSL_INIT_LOAD_CONFIG; the candidate's OPENSSL_init_crypto then runs the configuration load, and src/provider/conf.rs turns a providers section into a real provider activation (provider_conf_activate) whose module path can name an external DSO. Neither workload imports OSSL_PROVIDER_load, but that does not exclude a config-driven load inside libcrypto. The target set can therefore grow beyond the built-in provider, so A1 is not statically bounded.

A2.decision: resolved for the 13 audited sites; a separate RSA_METHOD residual is recorded
A2.why: the 13 sites dispatch built-in EVP_PKEY_METHOD/EVP_MD/EVP_CIPHER/BIO_METHOD/UI_METHOD/X509_LOOKUP_METHOD/CONF_METHOD tables; neither workload imports a setter for those families. The audit's import predicate omitted RSA_meth_*, and ssh does import RSA_meth_dup, RSA_meth_set1_name, RSA_meth_set_priv_enc and RSA_meth_set_priv_dec (its PKCS#11 RSA method). That installs application callbacks into an RSA_METHOD, so the broader statement 'no workload-supplied method table is registered' is false. None of the 13 A2 sites dispatches an RSA_METHOD, so this does not widen their immediate targets; the RSA_METHOD seam is reachable through the built-in RSA pkey-method implementation and is outside the 13. It is a retained residual for the consumer's overall safety, not an element-7 resolution.
A2.audit_gap: RSA_meth_dup/RSA_meth_set* were not in the audit's import-evidence list

O1.public_contract: CRYPTO_set_mem_functions(void *(*)(size_t,const char*,int), void *(*)(void*,size_t,const char*,int), void (*)(void*,const char*,int))
O1.runtime_fact_not_static_bound: the three globals are NULL in this configuration, so the cmp/cmov selects the in-image default_malloc/default_free; that is a runtime fact about this configuration, not a link-time bound. A process that installs hooks can reach a target outside this image.
O1.same_seam_elsewhere: inlined CRYPTO_free/CRYPTO_malloc selections in reachable code resolve through the static fallback and are outside the audited residual; they are not counted as O1 here (the audit's own 3-site scope)

full_lib_suite.venue_interaction: the test runtime::bio::owned::alloc_own_tests::alloc_own_refused_allocation_answers_none_and_releases_nothing calls CRYPTO_malloc(usize::MAX). With ASan's default allocator_may_return_null=0, ASan aborts with 'requested allocation size 0xffffffffffffffff ... exceeds maximum supported size'. Setting allocator_may_return_null=1 (the documented option for exercising allocation refusal) makes the test pass. This option is NOT set by forensics/tools/ms_asan.py; that is a tooling/config gap recorded here, not a product finding.

predicate_element_7.why: all R1/R2/R3/A2 sites are reported resolved, but 26 provider-configuration sites and 3 allocator-override sites remain unresolved in each binary. The provider sites are not statically bounded because configuration can load an external provider module; the allocator sites are the public CRYPTO_set_mem_functions seam. The element therefore still fails, on exactly those two classes and no others.
what_would_establish_it: exclude or bound config-driven provider-module loading for these two workloads (for example by proving the effective configuration cannot name a module, or by discharging the provider-config ABI as a bounded set)
establish the CRYPTO_set_mem_functions reachability predicate statically, or record O1 as an accepted ABI-open exception at the promotion gate

regressions_and_findings: The reachable-file set grew (ssh 333 -> 345; sshd 321 -> 340) because the new dlsym and table evidence admits precise edges the prior residual bound did not. The obligations remain 1 DISCHARGED, 0 BLOCKED, 0 UNKNOWN. The newly reachable provider cipher site is A1-open and is reported.

A1 is genuinely open: the audit's note that a config-driven load is 'not excluded' is confirmed, and the concrete path is SSL_CTX_new_ex -> OPENSSL_init_ssl (which adds OPENSSL_INIT_LOAD_CONFIG unconditionally in this candidate) -> OPENSSL_init_crypto -> provider_conf_activate. This is a compatibility-relevant divergence from the authority's default-config behavior only if the authority's default differs; the closure does not claim that.

A2 audit gap: the audit's import predicate did not include RSA_meth_*. ssh imports RSA_meth_dup/RSA_meth_set1_name/RSA_meth_set_priv_enc/RSA_meth_set_priv_dec and installs application callbacks in an RSA_METHOD. The 13 A2 sites are not RSA_METHOD dispatch, but the broader 'no workload-supplied method table' statement is false and is retained as a residual.

non_claims: This is not a SAFE_COMPATIBLE promotion and not a mechanism-wide SAFETY_DISCHARGED claim.
Predicate element 7 is not established; the receipt says precisely which classes remain open.
Miri is a research instrument, not the normative aliasing spec; the Stacked/Tree Borrows disagreement is recorded, not resolved by averaging.
ASan/TSan absence of a report is not a proof of memory safety; coverage is the named filters and the full lib suite, with the five pointer-identity failures classified as venue interactions.
The phase-2 ABI courts establish the structural distribution shell only; they are not semantic parity.

The closure's graph is an upper bound over the exact candidate DSOs; application code (including ssh's RSA_METHOD callbacks) is not a node in that graph, which is why the A2/RSA_METHOD residual is stated rather than converted into a target node.
